# Beads Workflow Context

> **Context Recovery**: Run `bd prime` after compaction, clear, or new session
> Hooks auto-call this in Claude Code and Codex when a beads workspace is resolved

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] 1. bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
[ ] 2. run quality gates        (tests, linters, builds when relevant)
[ ] 3. git status               (check what changed)
[ ] 4. follow active profile    (conservative: report handoff; team-maintainer: commit/sync/push if enabled)
```

**Policy:** Conservative is the default. Commit, sync, or push only when the active user, orchestrator, or repository profile grants that authority.

## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Default: do not commit, push, or run dolt remote sync without explicit authority. Team-maintainer behavior is opt-in and still subordinate to user/orchestrator instructions.
- Git workflow: conservative by default; commit/push only with explicit user/orchestrator or team-maintainer authority
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd dolt push` - Push beads to Dolt remote
- `bd dolt pull` - Pull beads from Dolt remote
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
git status                  # Check changed files
# Conservative/minimal/default: report status and proposed commands; wait for approval
# Team-maintainer opt-in only, unless current instructions forbid it:
# git add . && git commit -m "..."
# bd dolt push
# git push
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- lead-architect: Lead Architect role for a lead shop in the shopsystem framework. Invoke when the request requires selecting a message-type vehicle (assign_scenarios / request_bugfix / request_maintenance); composing and dispatching messages to BCs; verifying a BC's pre-state empirically; responding to a BC clarify on architecture, contracts, or decomposition; reconciling scenario registers; drafting ADRs; or making BC decomposition decisions. Do NOT invoke for Gherkin authoring or scope/vocabulary clarification — those belong to lead-po. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- lead-po: Lead PO role for a lead shop in the shopsystem framework. Invoke when the request requires authoring or sharpening Gherkin scenarios; drafting briefs or PDRs; or responding to a BC clarify on scope or vocabulary. Do NOT invoke for architecture decisions, message dispatch, or BC pre-state verification — those belong to lead-architect. Do NOT invoke for problem discovery, shaping, or option facilitation — those are conducted in the lead-pm main-session mode. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- bring-up-bc: Launch an already-scaffolded Bounded Context as a running, online container and verify it reaches the online state
- company-research: Build a cited, bounded intelligence brief on a competitor, peer product, or alternative framework — strategy, product philosophy, recent moves — to ground a brief/PDR in external reality instead of intuition. Use for the consumer-product competitive/market input to problem discovery, or to study a competing framework.
- create-bc: Create a new Bounded Context from scratch — scaffold, remote, manifest registration, and brokered launch — as the lead shop
- derisk-measurement-advisor: Scan a shaping candidate for risk across 10 dimensions — 4 internal (Desirability, Usability, Feasibility, Viability) and 6 external (PESTEL) — and triage each into act-now or track, so the candidate's rabbit-holes and risks name what to test before committing. Reach for it when a bet feels roadmap-ready and you want a structured "what could go wrong, internally and externally?"
- discovery-dialogue: Run the open, interactive discovery conversation that turns a directional or ambiguous prompt into a written, grounded intent record
- discovery-interview-prep: Design a customer discovery interview plan — research goal, target segment, access constraints, and a bias-resistant question set — so a discovery-dialogue turn produces real learning instead of confirmation. Use when the intent record rests on an assumed job that needs to be heard from a real user.
- discovery-process: The end-to-end discovery arc — frame, plan, research, synthesize, validate, decide — used to sequence a multi-turn discovery-dialogue and know which technique skill comes next. Use when a discovery is large enough to need staging rather than a single lens.
- eol-message: Empathetic end-of-life announcement for a retiring product or capability — acknowledges disruption, explains the change as progress, and gives a concrete migration path. Reach for it inside a product-narrative session, and specifically when a brief flips to status:retired.
- incoming-request-advisor: Decode an incoming request before responding — separate the literal ask from the job-behind-it, read the sender's power and stake, and surface hidden assumptions — so a request is classified by its real outcome, not its surface wording. Use at PM-mode entry, at the router's classification boundary, to decide whether a request needs a discovery-dialogue at all.
- jobs-to-be-done: Uncover the stable job a user is hiring the product to do — functional, social, emotional — plus their pains and gains, so intent anchors on a validated job instead of a feature request. Use during the discovery-dialogue when a request smells solution-shaped ("add X").
- opportunity-solution-tree: Move from a target outcome down through opportunities (problems) to candidate solutions to a chosen bet, so shaping commits the candidate to the right problem before it converges on a sketch. Reach for it when a request arrives outcome-shaped or solution-shaped and you need to keep "what are we moving?" upstream of "what do we build?"
- option-tradeoff: Frame two or more shaped options against each other, surface the tradeoffs, and run the deciding conversation with the product authority
- pol-probe: Design a Proof-of-Life probe — a lightweight, disposable experiment that tests one falsifiable hypothesis before expensive work — and land it in the candidate's evidence/experiments line. Reach for it when a shape rests on an assumption cheap enough to test in hours or days and honest enough to kill the bet if it fails.
- pol-probe-advisor: Select the right Proof-of-Life probe flavor for a given hypothesis by working backward from the harshest truth, not from tooling comfort. Reach for it inside shaping when you know an assumption needs testing but aren't sure whether it's a feasibility check, a task test, a narrative, a simulation, or a vibe-coded probe.
- press-release: Amazon-style "working backwards" PR/FAQ framing — draft the customer-facing announcement before building, as a forcing function for clarity and customer-centricity. Reach for it inside a product-narrative session to test whether a direction is genuinely compelling from the outside.
- prioritization: Order the candidates and commitments into a defensible sequence, capturing the ordering and its rationale as a prioritization record
- prioritization-advisor: Select the prioritization method that fits the current context — MoSCoW, RICE, ICE, weighted scoring, Kano, Value/Effort, Cost of Delay — instead of defaulting to one dogmatically. Reach for it inside a prioritization session before scoring anything, to pick the right lens for the stage, data, and decision at hand.
- problem-framing-canvas: Reframe a messy or solution-shaped request into a clear, bias-checked problem statement and a "How Might We" question before committing intent. Use inside the discovery-dialogue when you suspect you're about to solve the wrong problem.
- problem-space-mapping: Continuously maintain the map of the product's problem space so every candidate and intent has a place to hang, producing problem-space map revisions
- problem-statement: Turn a request or a raw job into a crisp, user-centered problem statement using the "I am / trying to / but / because / which makes me feel" frame, so intent names a person and a barrier, not a solution. Use inside the discovery-dialogue to fix the problem before any solutioning.
- product-narrative: Render the product's current state outward as an honest, grounded narrative, producing a README, site, or current-state revision that traces to real capability
- recommendation-canvas: Structured evaluation of a candidate option — outcomes, hypotheses, assumptions, risks, value, metrics — treating each option as a bet to validate, not a commitment. Reach for it inside an option-tradeoff session to turn a raw option list into a defensible pick with rationale.
- reconcile-and-close: Reconcile a completed BC dispatch by consuming its work_done outbox row and closing the corresponding bead as one atomic reconcile-and-close action via the reconcile-and-close executable wrapper
- shaping: Take a validated intent and drive a single candidate to shaped — bounded, de-risked, and ready for a commitment decision
- stakeholder-engagement-advisor: Plan engagement for one specific stakeholder — diagnose their profile and power/impact position, then tailor message, medium, cadence, and a named next action, planning both sides of the relationship. Use inside the discovery-dialogue when the intent hinges on a critical or resistant stakeholder whose input you must actually secure.
- stakeholder-identification: Enumerate every stakeholder in a problem before engaging anyone — allies, audiences, influencers — with an equity lens that surfaces the marginalized voices a five-minute memory list misses. Use inside the discovery-dialogue to be sure the intent isn't framed for only the loudest party.
- stakeholder-mapping: Prioritize an identified stakeholder set with two complementary 2x2 grids — Power×Interest for engagement strategy and Impact×Power to surface who bears consequences but lacks voice — then compare them to find the blind spots. Use inside the discovery-dialogue after identification to decide whose voice the intent must elevate.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- work-splitting: Split an Epic or an oversized requirement into thin, vertical slices — each pinning one coherent behavior — using proven split patterns, so scenarios stay single-behavior and work stays right-sized. Use when decomposing an Epic into scenarios, when a scenario carries multiple When/Then, or when an assigned unit is too big to build and review cleanly.
- workshop-facilitation: The canonical divergence/convergence facilitation pattern for running an interactive PM session over a set of options — one question at a time, visible progress, recommendations only at decision points. Reach for it inside an option-tradeoff session to structure how the dialogue is conducted.
- write-adr: Use when the author is authoring or creating a adr artifact — a generated guide that drives the adr to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the adr kind.
- write-brief: Use when the author is authoring or creating a brief artifact — a generated guide that drives the brief to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the brief kind.
- write-candidate: Use when the author is authoring or creating a candidate artifact — a generated guide that drives the candidate to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the candidate kind.
- write-current-state: Use when the author is authoring or creating a current-state artifact — a generated guide that drives the current-state to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the current-state kind.
- write-intent-record: Use when the author is authoring or creating a intent-record artifact — a generated guide that drives the intent-record to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the intent-record kind.
- write-pdr: Use when the author is authoring or creating a pdr artifact — a generated guide that drives the pdr to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the pdr kind.
- write-prioritization-record: Use when the author is authoring or creating a prioritization-record artifact — a generated guide that drives the prioritization-record to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the prioritization-record kind.
- write-session-record: Use when the author is authoring or creating a session-record artifact — a generated guide that drives the session-record to a validated document against the live shop-knowledge template and schema for the session-record kind.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

# Migration plan: rebaseline against the approved basis

Census run 2026-08-22 by four independent lanes over the live tree,
verifying the 2026-08-04 census where it overlapped and judging
everything after it fresh. This plan is the rebaseline's action table
plus the run order for `definition-chain-migration`; approving it starts
Phase 1.

## How to rule

**Vocabulary for this document.** A *chain* is a type's full definition
of good (typedef, guideline, fitness set, process, roles, compiled
skill); one `definition-chain-migration` run builds a chain and rewrites
that type's keepers through it. Actions: *keep-rewrite* — content still
binding, re-authored through the chain; *keep* — stays as-is, no rewrite
(scenarios and operational files); *retire* — value passed, moves to an
archive branch (never `main`); *terminal* — junk or never-advanced,
deleted or closed as never-accepted. The *F-codes* in reason cells are
the census's rewrite families — clusters of decision records that
collapse into one rewritten record each (F2 fleet … F15 licensing). The
*trust break* is the 2026-08-03 quality failure that triggered the
re-founding (intent-013).

**Ask 1 (block): approve the action table and run order.** Every row
carries its lane's one-line evidence. **Ask 2 (three rulings): the
authority calls below** — each has a recommendation and a default.

decision-chain run's review as an open item; nothing is retired or
deleted by silence.

# Cold read: /workspace/drafts/migration-plan.md (rev 2, 2026-08-22)

## 1. What is an F-code? Can F2–F15 be listed from this document alone?

Defined generically, yes:

> "The *F-codes* in reason cells are the census's rewrite families — clusters of decision records that collapse into one rewritten record each (F2 fleet … F15 licensing)."

An enumerated F2–F15 list: **UNANSWERABLE as an authoritative list.** Only F2 ("fleet") and F15 ("licensing") are named in the vocabulary. Everything else must be reverse-engineered from scattered reason cells, which yield approximate labels only: F3 "addressing/registry" (adr-006), F4 "canonicalization ownership" / "journal" (adr-019, adr-024/025), F5 "empirical-verification discipline" (adr-018), F6 "role system" (pdr-001), F7 "spike"/"doctrine-loop" (adr-029..032), F8 "CLI-vs-prose enforcement" / "spec-distribution" (adr-036/037), F9 "broker architecture" (adr-026), F10 "Footing bootstrap" (adr-040), F12 "fabro substrate" (adr-048), F13 "dagger substrate" (adr-052), F14 (adr-067 "mandatory rewrite; adopted fields only" — no plain-language name anywhere), F15 "licensing doctrine" (adr-061). **F11 never appears in the document** — I cannot tell whether it exists, was dissolved, or is a numbering gap. Whether these one-word cell fragments are the families' real definitions is a guess.

## 2. 87 rewritten records, or ~14 family records? Which passage settles it?

The vocabulary passage is the only one that speaks to output shape:

> "clusters of decision records that collapse into one rewritten record each"

and per-row cells agree in spirit: adr-001 "folds into F2 fleet record"; pdr-011 "collapses into ADR-018 discipline record"; adr-061 "collapses with adr-066". But the execution notes count inputs, not outputs:

> "Keeper counts by run: run 2 carries 87 decision records"

**The post-migration record count is UNANSWERABLE.** The vocabulary implies roughly one record per family (~13–14, given F2…F15 with F11 absent), but the document never states the output count, and several keep-rewrite rows carry **no F-code at all** (adr-002 "Contested fact resolved…", pdr-039 "Governing instrument…"), so I cannot tell whether every keeper joins a family, whether codeless keepers survive as standalone records, or how many records exist when run 2 finishes.

## 3. Where and when does the authority review each migrated artifact? What are the accept/reject options?

**UNANSWERABLE at the per-artifact level.** What the document does provide:

- Up-front bulk approval: "**Ask 1 (block): approve the action table and run order.** Every row carries its lane's one-line evidence."
- Three named rulings (Ask 2), with defaults: "Silence on a call is itself handled: the default carries it into the decision-chain run's review as an open item; nothing is retired or deleted by silence."
- A venue called "the chain review" / "the decision-chain review" that settles held items and even a standing policy question ("The chain review settles the standing kind-set question (ADR vs PDR boundary, RACI)…"; pdr-025: "family re-adjudicates at chain review").

But nothing says who conducts a chain review, whether the authority sees each rewritten record (or each family record, or each type), what evidence is presented, or what accept/reject/amend options exist per artifact, per type, or per family. The 27 retiring scenario pins, the 115 lane-D retires, and the 7 deleted junk trees appear to have **no post-approval review moment at all** — approval of Ask 1 is the review, and "Junk trees (`terminal`) delete at execution start."

## 4. Can execution begin the day of approval? What must exist before run 1?

The document says approval is the trigger: "approving it starts Phase 1." (**"Phase 1" appears exactly once and is never defined** — I assume it means run 1 plus the terminal deletions, since "Junk trees (`terminal`) delete at execution start.")

On whether definitions pre-exist: the vocabulary says chains are built **inside** each run — "one `definition-chain-migration` run builds a chain and rewrites that type's keepers through it" — and the run order shows chains in mixed states of pre-existence: run 1 "chain nearly complete"; run 4 "the session-record chain partly exists (handoff process approved)". So: **partially built, completed per run** — but no passage states what "nearly complete" lacks, what tools or processes must exist first, or any precondition checklist for run 1. Tools referenced as already existing: `bin/gen-scenario-refs` ("re-runs"), `bin/doctor` (in a reason cell). The `archive-retired` step is named but its mechanics are not. **Readiness criteria: UNANSWERABLE.**

## 5. What is "definition-chain-migration"? Its steps?

Everything the document tells you, assembled:

> "A *chain* is a type's full definition of good (typedef, guideline, fitness set, process, roles, compiled skill); one `definition-chain-migration` run builds a chain and rewrites that type's keepers through it."

plus two step names mentioned in passing: an "`archive-retired` step" ("retire mass moves to archive branches at each run's `archive-retired` step") and a "chain review" (venue for held authority calls and open items). That is the complete step inventory. Order of steps, entry/exit criteria, who performs each, what "compiled skill" means, and how a "rewrite through the chain" is actually performed: **UNANSWERABLE.** The document treats `definition-chain-migration` as an already-defined process living somewhere else.

## 6. Terms of art: defined vs assumed

**Defined in-document** (all in the "Vocabulary for this document" block or execution notes): *chain*, *keep-rewrite*, *keep*, *retire*, *terminal*, *F-codes* (generically), *trust break* ("the 2026-08-03 quality failure that triggered the re-founding (intent-013)"), and partially *archive branch* ("the memory-archive pattern: parentless branch, never on `main`").

**Used but never defined:** *lane* (A–D; four "independent lanes" — of what? people? agents? passes?), *keeper* (implied by keep-rewrite but never stated), *pin* (893 of them; the unit of the scenarios lane), *census* (the whole plan rests on it), *authority-call* (as an action value), *chain review*, *run*, *Phase 1*, *provenance spine* / "Spine root", *origin-cited* / origin-index, *doctrine loop* / "doctrine-loop exit", *kind-set question*, *RACI*, *pour / poured* (adr-057 "pour projection; poured .fabro pinned" is nearly opaque), *gate / gate green*, *hash* / "153-hash retirement" / "hashes re-mint", *dead letter*, *freeze* / "Freeze-paused", *memory close-out*, *rebaseline*, *BC*, *work_done*, *sc06*, *Footing*, *fabro*, *dagger*, *wall protocol*, *terminal state* (adr-045 "needs terminal state" — unrelated to the *terminal* action? unclear).

From your checklist specifically: **chain — defined; keeper — assumed; lane — assumed; pin — assumed; census — assumed; trust break — defined; attention architecture — does not appear in the document at all.**

## 7. References I cannot resolve or whose role I cannot determine

- **lead-jozud.2** — "the lead-jozud.2 evidence" (run 2). No idea what this is; it materially grounds a policy decision (kind-set/RACI).
- **intent-013** — named as "the governing instrument of the rebaseline" and the trust-break trigger, but its content is unknown; the whole plan claims authority under it.
- **pdr-039** — "flips accepted at doctrine-loop exit": both the flip mechanism and the doctrine loop are external.
- **sc06** — "sc06-deferral clause scrubbed at rewrite"; "the sc06 scenario body in the memory close-out". Unresolvable.
- **rebaseline-bill** — superseded predecessor (frontmatter + Appendix A); content unknown, so I cannot check what changed between plans.
- **drafts/artifact-system-restructuring.md** — "the initiative this plan executes" — role asserted, content unknown.
- **ID gaps: adr-003, adr-007, adr-044, pdr-008 are absent from a table claiming completeness** — I cannot tell whether they never existed, were already deleted, or were missed by the census. Same for **F11**.
- **brief-007** — "its anchored ADRs keep their content" — which ADRs? Unstated.
- External rulings/events relied on: the "2026-07-04 'no current use' ruling", the "2026-08-04 census", the "memory close-out", the "07-25" execution (brief-024, intent-006).
- Paths/files whose existence I must take on faith: `01-principles.md`, spec "02–06", `bc-manifest.yaml`, `bin/doctor`, `bin/gen-scenario-refs`, `scenario-refs/origin-index.txt`, `features/system-manifest`, `structurizr/`, both `docs/runbooks`.

## 8. Do the numbers reconcile?

I counted every printed row. Results:

- **Lane A: reconciles exactly.** 69 adr rows + 39 pdr rows = 108; retire = 7 adr + 10 pdr = 17; authority-call = 4 (adr-033, 046, 047, pdr-030); keep-rewrite = 87; terminal = 0. ✔

<result># Adversarial review — migration-plan.md rev 2

## A) Findings

Severity legend: **BLOCKER** = the plan cannot be executed (or lawfully approved) as written; **MAJOR** = execution would produce ungoverned or unverifiable results; **MINOR** = defect, containable.

**F1 — BLOCKER — The archive tool the process requires does not exist and the plan never asks for it.**
Evidence: `/home/vscode/basis-experiment/basis/processes/definition-chain-migration.md:104-107` — "The `archive-move` command in `archive-retired` is the archive contract tool **the migration plan's review must approve** … Until it exists the step blocks." `archive-move` is not in `/workspace/bin/` (contains only agent-vault-check, agent-vault-provision, check-knowledge-artifacts, doctor, gen-scenario-refs, ops-coordinates, shop-shell), not on PATH, and the string "archive-move" appears nowhere in `/workspace/drafts/migration-plan.md`. Ask 1 and Ask 2 (lines 35-41, 88-105) contain no approval of the archive contract.
Consequence: every run dead-ends at `archive-retired`; O3 unreachable; and the one review that is contractually supposed to approve the tool passes without approving it.

**F2 — BLOCKER — The approved process definition has a broken control flow: `derive-chain` has no `next`, so `exemplar-rewrite` is unreachable.**
Evidence: `definition-chain-migration.md:132-140` — the `derive-chain` step ends at `run:` with no `next:`; every other non-terminal step has one. The compiled mermaid (lines 64-77) faithfully shows it: `build_chain --> derive_chain` then nothing; `exemplar_rewrite --> authority_review` has no inbound edge. The compiler reproduced the bug; the "compiles and screens" check (line 267) passed a process whose flow cannot reach its own review loop.
Consequence: run 1 halts after chain derivation; no exemplar, no authority review, no approval — structurally, per the definition, nothing can be rewritten. This is the strongest literal form of David's objection.

**F3 — BLOCKER — The plan's retire/terminal mass has no process that moves it.**
Evidence: plan lines 85-86 "Junk trees (`terminal`) delete at execution start; retire mass moves to archive branches at each run's `archive-retired` step" vs. `definition-chain-migration.md:242-247` — `archive-retired` takes input `demoted` only, and `demoted` is produced solely by `rewrite-keepers` (keepers that failed rewrite). The 163 pre-decided retires and 14 terminals are never in `keepers`, never in `demoted`, and no other process exists in `basis/processes/` for deletion, closure ("closed as never-accepted", plan line 28-29), or scenario-file retirement (run 6, lines 82-84, is explicitly "no chain needed" — i.e., not a `definition-chain-migration` run at all, under a heading that says "one `definition-chain-migration` run per type", line 65).
Consequence: the bulk of the plan's effect (177 of 318 records) is an orphan activity — `no-orphan-activities` violation; executed, it would be an ungoverned mass mutation; unexecuted, the plan's stated outcome never occurs.

**F4 — BLOCKER — The F-code rewrite families are defined only in a document this plan retires, and no process input can carry them.**
Evidence: plan line 29-31 names only "F2 fleet … F15 licensing"; the full family map (membership, target record counts, F1 folding, F11 empty) exists solely at `/workspace/drafts/rebaseline-bill.md:55-69` — which the plan supersedes (frontmatter line 5) and retires (Appendix A, line 358: "rebaseline-bill (superseded by this plan)"). Meanwhile the process signature is `parameters: [artifact_type, keepers]` (`definition-chain-migration.md:111`) with `keepers: string[]` — there is no data slot through which the collapse map, or any reason-cell directive ("folds into F2", line 111; "sc06-deferral clause scrubbed at rewrite", line 132; "recover falsified date", line 165; "collapses with adr-066", line 168; "may fold into F9", line 156; "re-verify deferred primitive first", line 117), can lawfully enter `rewrite-keepers`.
Consequence: run 2 must either load a retired, ungoverned document into the generating context (`governed-context` violation) or silently drop the operative rewrite instructions the authority approved. Both are failure. Also directly: (a) the F2–F15 list is defined nowhere the plan governs; (b) answered below in F5/F6.

**F5 — BLOCKER — Collapse decisions are made before the definition that would license them exists (decide-before-define).**
Evidence: the plan fixes many→one collapses now ("clusters of decision records that collapse into one rewritten record each", lines 30-31; 87 keepers → ~14 families) while the decision-record chain is empty: `lint_basis.py --derive-chain decision-record` returns all-empty, status draft (empirically run; only `decision-brief` — a presentation-request type, not the ADR/PDR type, see `basis/artifacts/decision-brief.md:16-25` — has a complete approved chain). What one decision record may carry — its scope, size, one-decision-or-many — is exactly what the run-2 typedef/guideline/fitness will define; the collapse pre-empts it. Violated principle: **`define-good-up-front`** (the activity — collapse-mapping — operates with no stated definition of good), with `governed-context` as the accessory.
Consequence: approving Ask 1 approves record granularity for a type whose definition of good does not exist; when the chain review later defines it, either the approved table is wrong or the chain is retro-fitted to the table — the check would be shaped by the thing it checks.

**F6 — BLOCKER — Run structure contradicts the process's scope rule, and the contradiction is circular.**
Evidence: `definition-chain-migration.md:40-42` — "one run migrates one artifact type." Run 2 bundles adr+pdr while explicitly deferring whether they are one type or two into that same run's review ("the chain review settles the standing kind-set question (ADR vs PDR boundary, RACI)", plan lines 71-74). Run 4 bundles four types (intent, candidate, brief, session; line 78). Run 3 bundles spec chapters, README, current-state, and a `structurizr/` DSL directory (lines 75-77) under a type ("framework spec") with no typedef anywhere in `basis/artifacts/`.
Consequence: the keeper partition (87 / 28 / …) is fixed by a type boundary that the run itself is supposed to decide — if the review splits ADR from PDR (or session from brief), the approved run structure and keeper counts are invalidated mid-run. The run order cannot be approved until the type set is at least provisionally ruled.

**F7 — BLOCKER — Vocabulary: "kind" seven times, against an approved glossary term and a numbered authority ruling.**
Evidence: plan lines 72, 181, 215, 228, 233, 245, 307 vs `basis/glossary.md:21-22` ("**artifact type** — … Not 'kind'") and `basis/README.md` R9 (~lines 243-250): "'kind', coined beside the already-defined 'artifact type', is removed everywhere" — described as `use-defined-terms`' "first conviction."
Consequence: the authority cannot approve, in the first Phase-1 instrument, the exact term whose removal was his first recorded ruling; approval as written re-violates R9. (Trivial to fix; blocking only in the sense that the document is unapprovable as written.)
Extended sweep, same principle: **"keep"** and **"authority-call"** are used as actions (plan lines 26-27; rows 141, 153, 154, 208, 263, 311) but `glossary.md:84-85` closes the action enum at "keep-rewrite, retire, or terminal"; "authority-call" is not even in the plan's own Actions vocabulary (lines 25-29); "keep (regenerate)" (line 315) is a sixth variant. Undefined terms also used: *lane*, *census*, *pins*, *origin-cited*, *provenance spine* (line 348), *trust break* (in-doc gloss only), *RACI* (line 72, bare initialism).

**F8 — MAJOR — The authority's review surface over the mass rewrite is undefined: "the attention architecture" exists nowhere.**
Evidence: `definition-chain-migration.md:236` — "authority spot-checks per the attention architecture" — the phrase's only occurrence in the entire basis and workspace (verified by grep). Trace of actual authority touchpoints per run: (1) `authority-review` (lines 158-167): the chain plus **one** exemplar keeper, verdict clean/tradeoffs/findings, round cap 3; (2) `approve-chain` (lines 202-213): stamps the chain documents; (3) undefined spot-checks during `rewrite-keepers`. So the authority rules **per chain** (once) and **per one exemplar** (once); **per family** — never as such; **per artifact** — only via an undefined sampling clause. For run 2 that means ~87 keepers collapsing into family records with exactly one authority-inspected specimen and no defined sample thereafter.
Consequence: David's question 2(c) has no answer in the material because the material doesn't contain one. This needs an authority-defined attention contract before run 2 at the latest.

Confirmed — your read is exactly right, and here's the full picture:

**The basis lives only on the branch.** `experiment/new-basis` adds the entire `basis/` tree (38 files) and nothing else; `main` has none of it. Meanwhile `main` already carries **generated projections whose sources are on the branch**: the compiled principles rendering in `.claude/shop/principles.md` and the compiled skills — including `stakeholder-presentation`, whose frontmatter says `source: basis/processes/stakeholder-presentation.md`, a path that doesn't exist on `main`. That's the inconsistent state you're sensing: outputs were promoted to the operating tree while their single sources stayed on the branch — a straight `single-source-of-truth` break, and the adversarial review flagged the same thing from the other end (its required-condition #13: the plan never says where chains and rewritten records land, ending in the ruling "when does the basis become `main`?"). You've now ruled that: **the basis merges to `main` before anything else proceeds.**

The merge itself is clean by construction — the branch is purely additive (only `basis/` plus a trivial `.vscode/settings.json`), no overlapping files, so no conflicts. One sequencing point: the basis-repair agent is mid-flight *on the branch right now* (fixing the broken `derive-chain` flow, adding the `action-table` channel and the `corpus-close-out` process draft). I'll let it land and push its branch commit, then do a single merge of `experiment/new-basis` into `main` and push — otherwise we'd merge twice around its work. The rev 3 plan agent works only on `drafts/migration-plan.md` on `main`, which the branch doesn't touch, so it's unaffected.

**And to close out your stakeholder-presentation question** (my answer was cut off): the trigger matches — the skill should have run for both rev 2 and my session-start delivery. It didn't because its activation is `model-judged` (advisory; nothing gates delivery on it), and both deliveries bypassed it. For rev 2, the process was demonstrably not run to completion: commit `c872505` contains only the 393-line plan — no decision-brief (the plan is ~10× over the compose budget that exists precisely so you're never handed a document like that), no annex structure, and **no round log**, which the deliver step requires as the verified-by record. "Cold-read verified" was an unwitnessed assertion; the repairs listed in the commit show the read checked internal consistency, not the required per-ask decidability — today's isolated cold read returned *cannot-decide* on the core asks. This session, I then trusted the record's "cold-read verified" claim instead of re-running the check at delivery. The fix has two parts, and both are in flight: rev 3 will be delivered *through* a full stakeholder-presentation run (brief + fresh cold read + round log attached), and the activation gap — a `model-judged` check that failed twice on the material it exists for — is a process finding I'll file for the review: authority-facing delivery needs a process-level gate, not model discretion.

34	## How to rule
35	
36	**Ask 1 (block): approve the action table, the family nominations, and
37	the run order.** Every row carries its lane's one-line evidence.
38	Approval fixes three things: which records are keepers, which retire,
39	and which are terminal (the census rows); the sequence of the
40	per-type runs; and the F-family groupings **as nominations only**.
41	Approval does NOT fix: the final granularity of rewritten records
42	(decided at the run-2 chain review, after the decision-record typedef,
43	guideline, and fitness set exist — see Appendix B), the final
44	artifact-type set, or the archive execution (its contract is a pending
45	ruling). The three record-level authority calls below each carry a
46	recommendation and a default; silence on a call is itself handled — the
47	default carries it into the decision-chain run's review as an open
48	item; nothing is retired or deleted by silence.
49	
50	The remaining structural rulings are listed under **Open rulings**
51	below. They will be finalized in a separate decision-brief; this plan
52	carries each only as a one-line question with a recommendation and a
53	default.
54	
55	### Vocabulary for this document
56	
57	Terms marked (g) are defined in the approved glossary
58	(`basis/glossary.md` — the basis merged to `main` at c5f1495 and is
59	the operating tree; `experiment/new-basis` is history); the rest are
60	defined here for this document.
61	
62	- **chain** (g: definition chain) — a type's full definition of good:
63	  six linked definitions — typedef, guideline, fitness set, process,
64	  roles, compiled skill. One `definition-chain-migration` run builds a
65	  chain and rewrites that type's keepers through it.
66	- **chain review** — the authority review of a run's chain and
67	  exemplar inside that run (the `authority_review` / `route_review`
68	  steps of the process); verdicts and round cap in "The authority's
69	  review surface" below.
70	- **keeper** (g) — a record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
71	  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
72	- **Actions** — the enum covering every action cell: *keep-rewrite* —
73	  content still binding, re-authored through the chain; *keep* — stays
74	  as-is, no rewrite (scenarios and operational files); *retire* —
75	  value passed, moves to the archive branch (never `main`); *terminal*
76	  — junk or never-advanced, deleted or closed as never-accepted.
77	  (Vocabulary note: the glossary's `action` enum is keep-rewrite /
78	  retire / terminal; this plan extends it with *keep* for records
79	  already in native format — flagged for glossary amendment.)
80	- **authority-call** — a row MARKER, not an action: the row awaits an
81	  authority ruling and neither rewrites nor retires until ruled.
82	- **lane** — one of the four independent census passes (A decisions,
83	  B PM records, C scenarios, D docs/findings/drafts/root/junk); each
84	  lane read the tree independently and its evidence stands per row.
85	- **census** — the four-lane read-only survey of the live tree whose
86	  rows this action table carries; this plan's tables are the census.
87	- **pin** — one anchored `@scenario_hash:` tag line in `features/`,
88	  fixing one canonical scenario block. Pins are counted separately
89	  from records and never enter a record total.
90	- **F-codes / rewrite families** — clusters of decision records
91	  NOMINATED to collapse into a small number of rewritten records.
92	  Nominations only: final record granularity is decided at the run-2
93	  chain review. The authoritative family map is Appendix B.
94	- **RACI** — the standard responsibility matrix (Responsible /
95	  Accountable / Consulted / Informed); here, the open question of
96	  which role owns which record type, under investigation as
97	  lead-jozud.2 (glossed below).
98	- **trust break** — the 2026-08-03 quality failure that triggered the
99	  re-founding (intent-013, the re-founding instrument: the authority's
100	  recorded direction to re-found the typed-artifact system in four
101	  phases after finding systemic quality failures).
102	- **provenance spine** — the `derives-from`/`derived-by` edge graph
103	  rooted at intent records, along which every PM record traces to a
104	  recorded want.

107	  over review iterations instead of one-shot authoring.

## How to rule

**Ask 1 (block): approve the action table, the family nominations, and
the run order.** Every row carries its lane's one-line evidence.
Approval fixes three things: which records are keepers, which retire,
and which are terminal (the census rows); the sequence of the
per-type runs; and the F-family groupings **as nominations only**.
Approval does NOT fix: the final granularity of rewritten records
(decided at the run-2 chain review, after the decision-record typedef,
guideline, and fitness set exist — see Appendix B), the final
artifact-type set, or the archive execution (its contract is a pending
ruling). The three record-level authority calls below each carry a
recommendation and a default; silence on a call is itself handled — the
default carries it into the decision-chain run's review as an open
item; nothing is retired or deleted by silence.

The remaining structural rulings are listed under **Open rulings**
below. They will be finalized in a separate decision-brief; this plan
carries each only as a one-line question with a recommendation and a
default.

### Vocabulary for this document

Terms marked (g) are defined in the approved glossary
(`basis/glossary.md` — the basis merged to `main` at c5f1495 and is
the operating tree; `experiment/new-basis` is history); the rest are
defined here for this document.

- **chain** (g: definition chain) — a type's full definition of good:
  six linked definitions — typedef, guideline, fitness set, process,
  roles, compiled skill. One `definition-chain-migration` run builds a
  chain and rewrites that type's keepers through it.
- **chain review** — the authority review of a run's chain and
  exemplar inside that run (the `authority_review` / `route_review`
  steps of the process); verdicts and round cap in "The authority's
  review surface" below.
- **keeper** (g) — a record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
- **Actions** — the enum covering every action cell: *keep-rewrite* —
  content still binding, re-authored through the chain; *keep* — stays
  as-is, no rewrite (scenarios and operational files); *retire* —
  value passed, moves to the archive branch (never `main`); *terminal*
  — junk or never-advanced, deleted or closed as never-accepted.
  (Vocabulary note: the glossary's `action` enum is keep-rewrite /
  retire / terminal; this plan extends it with *keep* for records
  already in native format — flagged for glossary amendment.)
- **authority-call** — a row MARKER, not an action: the row awaits an
  authority ruling and neither rewrites nor retires until ruled.
- **lane** — one of the four independent census passes (A decisions,
  B PM records, C scenarios, D docs/findings/drafts/root/junk); each
  lane read the tree independently and its evidence stands per row.
- **census** — the four-lane read-only survey of the live tree whose
  rows this action table carries; this plan's tables are the census.
- **pin** — one anchored `@scenario_hash:` tag line in `features/`,
  fixing one canonical scenario block. Pins are counted separately
  from records and never enter a record total.
- **F-codes / rewrite families** — clusters of decision records
  NOMINATED to collapse into a small number of rewritten records.
  Nominations only: final record granularity is decided at the run-2
  chain review. The authoritative family map is Appendix B.
- **RACI** — the standard responsibility matrix (Responsible /
  Accountable / Consulted / Informed); here, the open question of
  which role owns which record type, under investigation as
  lead-jozud.2 (glossed below).
- **trust break** — the 2026-08-03 quality failure that triggered the
  re-founding (intent-013, the re-founding instrument: the authority's
  recorded direction to re-found the typed-artifact system in four
  phases after finding systemic quality failures).
- **provenance spine** — the `derives-from`/`derived-by` edge graph
  rooted at intent records, along which every PM record traces to a
  recorded want.
- **doctrine loop** — the Phase-0 iterative doctrine-capture loop
  under intent-013 (opened sess-2026-08-04-a), which produced pdr-039
  over review iterations instead of one-shot authoring.

### External references glossed

- **lead-jozud.2** — the merged artifact-type-set + RACI
  investigation (see `sessions/sess-2026-08-05-a.md`): which record
  types survive, the ADR/PDR boundary, and role ownership per type.
- **sc06** — a deferred scenario body (hash 5174e405a19358fa, per
  adr-024 D2); now carried verbatim by backlog item lead-df2pj.
- **the 153-hash prior census (2026-08-04)** — the scenario-retirement
  lane of the superseded rebaseline-bill, which proposed retiring 153
  scenario hashes across 30 files; this plan dissolves most of it (see

# Brief 026 — Rebaseline migration: rule on rev 3 and its preconditions

## The answer first

You returned the migration plan with findings; the adversarial review
you directed then found worse: the approved migration process itself had
a broken step flow that made any rewrite structurally impossible, the
163 retiring records had no process that moves them, and the plan was
deciding record collapses before any definition existed to license
them. All of that is repaired and landed as drafts on `main` — what
remains is your ruling. **Recommendation: approve the plan (ask 1) and
the four repaired definitions (ask 2), ratify the archive contract
(ask 3), and let asks 4–7 resolve by their stated defaults.** Asks 1
and 2 gate run 1; ask 3 gates any archiving or deletion; asks 4–7
resolve on silence, each by the default stated with it. Nothing is
retired, deleted, or rewritten by silence alone.

What approval does and does not fix: ask 1 fixes which records are
kept, retired, or terminal, the run order, and the rewrite-family
groupings **as nominations only** — final record granularity (your
"collapse into 15 overloads an ADR" concern) is decided at the run-2
chain review, after the decision-record definition exists to say what
one record may carry. Each migration run first builds and proves the
type's definition ("chain": typedef, guideline, fitness set, process,
roles, compiled skill), takes your review of the chain plus one real
rewritten exemplar (up to 3 rounds, then it parks), and only after your
approval mass-rewrites. The definitions do not pre-exist — building
them is each run's first act, and the plan now says so.

## Asks

**1. Approve migration plan rev 3 as a block.** *Recommend: approve.*
Evidence: every count machine-verified against disk (310 records:
130 keep-rewrite, 5 keep, 163 retire, 7 terminal, 5 awaiting rulings;

# Brief 026 — Rebaseline migration: rule on rev 3 and its preconditions

## The answer first

You returned the migration plan with findings; the adversarial review
you directed then found worse: the approved migration process itself had
a broken step flow that made any rewrite structurally impossible, the
163 retiring records had no process that moves them, and the plan was
deciding record collapses before any definition existed to license
them. All of that is repaired and landed as drafts on `main` — what
remains is your ruling. **Recommendation: approve the plan (ask 1) and
the four repaired definitions (ask 2), ratify the archive contract
(ask 3), and let asks 4–7 resolve by their stated defaults.** Asks 1
and 2 gate run 1; ask 3 gates any archiving or deletion; asks 4–7
resolve on silence, each by the default stated with it. Nothing is
retired, deleted, or rewritten by silence alone.

What approval does and does not fix: ask 1 fixes which records are
kept, retired, or terminal, the run order, and the rewrite-family
groupings **as nominations only** — final record granularity (your
"collapse into 15 overloads an ADR" concern) is decided at the run-2
chain review, after the decision-record definition exists to say what
one record may carry. Each migration run first builds and proves the
type's definition ("chain": typedef, guideline, fitness set, process,
roles, compiled skill), takes your review of the chain plus one real
rewritten exemplar (up to 3 rounds, then it parks), and only after your
approval mass-rewrites. The definitions do not pre-exist — building
them is each run's first act, and the plan now says so.

## Asks

**1. Approve migration plan rev 3 as a block.** *Recommend: approve.*
Evidence: every count machine-verified against disk (310 records:
130 keep-rewrite, 5 keep, 163 retire, 7 terminal, 5 awaiting rulings;
893 scenario pins: 860 keep, 27 retire, 6 riding ask 6's third call);
rev 2's arithmetic errors, "kind" usages, unexplained F-codes, and
opaque references are all corrected — the family map is now the plan's
own Appendix B. *Default: the plan stays draft; nothing proceeds.*

**2. Re-approve the four repaired definitions.** The migration process
(`basis/processes/definition-chain-migration.md`) amended: its
`derive-chain` step had no exit — the flow dead-ended before your
review, so no rewrite could ever have run — and it gained a governed
`actions` input so your approved per-record directives reach the
rewrite step through a defined channel, not a retired document. New:
`corpus-close-out` (the mechanical process that moves the retire and
terminal mass) and two supporting data types. All four sit on `main`
as drafts. *Recommend: approve all four.* Evidence: whole-basis lint
passes; the flow fix is visible in the compiled diagram. *Default: no
run starts.*

**3. Ratify the archive contract.** One parentless branch
`archive/migration-2026-08` holding retired files verbatim (the same
pattern as the memory archive you approved in R22), never on `main`,
plus snapshot tag `pre-migration` before any terminal deletion, and the
`archive-move` tool built to that spec before first use. *Recommend:
ratify.* Evidence: contract specced once in `corpus-close-out`;
terminal deletions are recoverable from the tag. *Default: nothing
archives and nothing is deleted; the mass stays frozen in place.*

**4. Attention contract for the mass rewrite.** How much of your
attention does each run's rewrite step get? *Recommend: per-family
sign-off before a family record is finalized, plus a spot-check of
every 10th rewritten record, plus a veto window before each run's
archive stage.* Evidence: rev 2 gave you one exemplar per run and cited
an "attention architecture" defined nowhere. *Default: every rewritten
record awaits your explicit sign-off — costlier, safer.*

**5. Provisional artifact-type set for runs 2–4.** *Recommend: run 2
builds one provisional decision-record chain and settles the ADR/PDR
boundary at its own chain review (the lead-jozud.2 investigation — the
open artifact-type-set and role-ownership question); run 4 carries the
current PM type names provisionally.* Evidence: the run partition
cannot wait on the final type set without circularity. *Default: the
recommendation, with any later type merge re-typing records
mechanically at close-out.*

**6. Three record-level calls.** (a) adr-033, a BC-local architect
role never realized — *recommend retire*; (b) adr-046, a
certificate-authority exemption the record says was removed but the
code still carries — *recommend retire; the as-built behavior gets its
decision fresh*; (c) the system-BOM bundle (adr-047 + pdr-030 +
brief-015 + 6 scenario pins), pinned yet unrealized for months —
*recommend retire the records and file one backlog item carrying the
intent verbatim.* *Default: any unruled call rides into the run-2
chain review as an open item.*

**7. Done-standard.** *Recommend: accept the plan's "What demonstrates
done" — per run: chain approved, rewritten records pass the type's
fitness set, lint clean; for the migration: the running system
demonstrates it (skills and renderings regenerate and load, gate and
lint green over the whole baseline, primers cite only rewritten
records, close-out report shows zero unaccounted rows).* Evidence:
counts and status stamps alone are exactly what the delivery-verified
principle rejects. *Default: the per-run minimum stands; the
migration-level standard is deferred to close-out review.*

## Deferred (notes, not asks)

- The plan's own type, `migration-plan`, has no typedef; it is excluded
  from its own census. Default: recorded as an open bootstrap-exception
  finding in the review ledger.
- The stakeholder-presentation activation gap (this brief's producing
  process was bypassed twice for this material) is filed as a finding
  under the review conversation; its fix comes to a later review.

## Annex

Full plan: [drafts/migration-plan.md](../drafts/migration-plan.md)
(rev 3) — action tables, run order, entry conditions, review surface,
family map. Optional; every ask above is decidable from this brief.

content.text:
# Cold-read report — brief-026.md

Read: `/workspace/briefs/brief-026.md` only. No annex, no repo, no prior rounds.

## Rubric 1 — Decidability per ask

*"Could a reader make every numbered decision using only this document?"* — Mostly, with two structural exceptions where the object being approved lives outside the document.

| Ask | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Approve plan rev 3 as a block | **wobbly** | The decision is over the plan's contents — per-record actions, run order, family map ("Appendix B") — but only counts and shape appear here. The brief asserts "every count machine-verified against disk"; the reader must either trust that sentence or open the annex the brief calls optional. A block-approval of a document summarized in ~15 lines is decidable only by proxy. |
| 2. Re-approve four repaired definitions | **wobbly** | The four artifacts are named and their deltas described in one clause each ("gained a governed `actions` input"), but the repaired text is on `main`, not here. Evidence ("lint passes; flow fix visible in the compiled diagram") is a claim, not a showing. Decidable if the reader accepts the description as the thing approved. |
| 3. Ratify archive contract | **confident** | The contract's full substance is in the ask itself: branch name, verbatim files, never on `main`, snapshot tag before terminal deletion, tool built to spec before first use, plus the reader's own R22 precedent. |
| 4. Attention contract | **confident** | Both options fully stated in-line (per-family sign-off + every-10th spot-check + veto window, vs. all-records sign-off default), with the risk rationale. Self-contained. |
| 5. Provisional type set | **confident** | The circularity rationale and the resolution venue (run-2 chain review) are both in the ask; lead-jozud.2 is glossed at first mention. |
| 6. Three record-level calls | **wobbly** | 6a and 6c are decidable (claims are one clause each, but retire is recoverable per ask 3, so the stakes fit the evidence). 6b is the wobble: "the as-built behavior gets its decision fresh" names no venue, owner, or filed item — retiring a record while its behavior still lives in code, with the replacement decision left hanging, needs outside context to rule on comfortably. |
| 7. Done-standard | **confident** | The standard itself is reproduced in the ask; the evidence ties it to a principle the reader owns; the default cleanly splits per-run from migration-level. |

No ask is **cannot-decide**. Asks 1 and 2 need outside context in the strict sense (the artifacts being approved); ask 6b needs it in a narrow sense (where the fresh decision lands).

## Rubric 2 — Recommendation in paragraph 1

**Yes.** Quote: "**Recommendation: approve the plan (ask 1) and the four repaired definitions (ask 2), ratify the archive contract (ask 3), and let asks 4–7 resolve by their stated defaults.**"

## Rubric 3 — Unglossed proper nouns

**Empty list — pass.** Checked: "chain" (glossed parenthetically), F2–F15 (glossed at first mention), `corpus-close-out` / `action-table` / `close-out-report` (each glossed), R22 (located in the review ledger and framed as the reader's own ruling), `archive-move` (glossed), lead-jozud.2 (glossed appositively), adr-033 / adr-046 (glossed), system-BOM (glossed, including the acronym), "attention architecture" (deliberately quoted as rev 2's undefined term). Borderline but passing: adr-047, pdr-030, brief-015 carry no individual glosses, covered only collectively by the bundle gloss in 6c; "stakeholder-presentation" is glossed only obliquely as "the producing process."

## Rubric 4 — Recommendation / evidence / default per ask

**All seven pass.** Every ask carries an explicit *Recommend*, an *Evidence* clause, and an italicized *Default*. No fails to cite. (Quality varies — ask 2's evidence is assertion-only, ask 6's is one clause per call — but presence is what this assertion tests.)

## Rubric 5 — Gate vs. silence stated?

**Yes.** Cite: "Asks 1 and 2 gate run 1; ask 3 gates any archiving or deletion; asks 4–7 resolve on silence, each by the default stated with it." (Paragraph 1.) Minor caveat: this sentence lives in "The answer first," not in the Asks section itself — the ask set proper never restates which of its members gate.

## Stumbles in reading order

1. **"5 awaiting rulings" (ask 1) is never linked to ask 6.** I had to count ask 6's records myself (a=1, b=1, c=3) to verify the 5 reconcile. The 6 scenario pins get an explicit "ask 6c below" pointer; the 5 records don't.
2. **"Ask 1 fixes which records are kept, retired, or terminal, the run order, and the rewrite-family groupings as nominations only"** — reread required: does "as nominations only" scope over all three list items or just the family groupings? If keep/retire/terminal is *fixed* by ask 1, ask 6's separate rulings on five of those records sit in tension; if it's all nominations, "fixes" is the wrong verb.
3. **Counting the "four" in ask 2** takes parsing: one amended process, one new process, two new data types — the enumeration is buried in prose ("New: … and its two supporting data types") and I counted twice.
4. **Ask 6b's "gets its decision fresh"** — guessed at where/when; nothing is filed, unlike 6c which files a backlog item.
5. **Ask 5's default ("the recommendation, with any later type merge re-typing records mechanically at close-out")** — a default that equals the recommendation plus an unstated-elsewhere rider; reread to confirm silence and approval differ only by nothing.
6. **`verified-by: pending`** in front-matter only makes sense after reaching the last Deferred bullet — a forward reference, resolved 130 lines later.

## Overload verdict

**Yes — rulable in one short sitting.** ~140 lines, seven asks of which four (3, 4, 5, 7) are fully self-contained policy choices, two (1, 2) reduce to trusting a stated verification, and one (6) is three small calls. Paragraph 1 gives a single-sentence fast path, defaults make silence safe, and the gating sentence tells the reader the minimum ruling (asks 1–3) needed to unblock work. The densest moments (ask 1's census clause, ask 5) slow but don't stall.

## Top three changes

1. **Close the census loop in ask 1:** point "5 awaiting rulings" at ask 6 explicitly, and rewrite "fixes … as nominations only" to say unambiguously which classifications block-approval makes final and which remain nominations.
2. **Give 6b's orphaned behavior a landing spot:** name where the as-built certificate-authority behavior "gets its decision fresh" (a filed backlog item, mirroring 6c, or the run-2 open-item list) so retiring the record doesn't leave live code undocumented on a promise.
3. **Put the gating sentence on the ask set itself:** repeat "gates run 1 / gates archiving / resolves on silence" as a tag on each ask header (or a line atop the Asks section), so the resolution rules travel with the asks rather than only in the preamble.

VERDICT: findings

## Rubric 1 — Decidability per ask

*"Could a reader make every numbered decision using only this document?"* — Mostly, with two structural exceptions where the object being approved lives outside the document.

| Ask | Verdict | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Approve plan rev 3 as a block | **wobbly** | The decision is over the plan's contents — per-record actions, run order, family map ("Appendix B") — but only counts and shape appear here. The brief asserts "every count machine-verified against disk"; the reader must either trust that sentence or open the annex the brief calls optional. A block-approval of a document summarized in ~15 lines is decidable only by proxy. |
| 2. Re-approve four repaired definitions | **wobbly** | The four artifacts are named and their deltas described in one clause each ("gained a governed `actions` input"), but the repaired text is on `main`, not here. Evidence ("lint passes; flow fix visible in the compiled diagram") is a claim, not a showing. Decidable if the reader accepts the description as the thing approved. |
| 3. Ratify archive contract | **confident** | The contract's full substance is in the ask itself: branch name, verbatim files, never on `main`, snapshot tag before terminal deletion, tool built to spec before first use, plus the reader's own R22 precedent. |
| 4. Attention contract | **confident** | Both options fully stated in-line (per-family sign-off + every-10th spot-check + veto window, vs. all-records sign-off default), with the risk rationale. Self-contained. |
| 5. Provisional type set | **confident** | The circularity rationale and the resolution venue (run-2 chain review) are both in the ask; lead-jozud.2 is glossed at first mention. |
| 6. Three record-level calls | **wobbly** | 6a and 6c are decidable (claims are one clause each, but retire is recoverable per ask 3, so the stakes fit the evidence). 6b is the wobble: "the as-built behavior gets its decision fresh" names no venue, owner, or filed item — retiring a record while its behavior still lives in code, with the replacement decision left hanging, needs outside context to rule on comfortably. |
| 7. Done-standard | **confident** | The standard itself is reproduced in the ask; the evidence ties it to a principle the reader owns; the default cleanly splits per-run from migration-level. |

No ask is **cannot-decide**. Asks 1 and 2 need outside context in the strict sense (the artifacts being approved); ask 6b needs it in a narrow sense (where the fresh decision lands).

## Rubric 2 — Recommendation in paragraph 1

**Yes.** Quote: "**Recommendation: approve the plan (ask 1) and the four repaired definitions (ask 2), ratify the archive contract (ask 3), and let asks 4–7 resolve by their stated defaults.**"

## Rubric 3 — Unglossed proper nouns

**Empty list — pass.** Checked: "chain" (glossed parenthetically), F2–F15 (glossed at first mention), `corpus-close-out` / `action-table` / `close-out-report` (each glossed), R22 (located in the review ledger and framed as the reader's own ruling), `archive-move` (glossed), lead-jozud.2 (glossed appositively), adr-033 / adr-046 (glossed), system-BOM (glossed, including the acronym), "attention architecture" (deliberately quoted as rev 2's undefined term). Borderline but passing: adr-047, pdr-030, brief-015 carry no individual glosses, covered only collectively by the bundle gloss in 6c; "stakeholder-presentation" is glossed only obliquely as "the producing process."

## Rubric 4 — Recommendation / evidence / default per ask

**All seven pass.** Every ask carries an explicit *Recommend*, an *Evidence* clause, and an italicized *Default*. No fails to cite. (Quality varies — ask 2's evidence is assertion-only, ask 6's is one clause per call — but presence is what this assertion tests.)

## Rubric 5 — Gate vs. silence stated?

**Yes.** Cite: "Asks 1 and 2 gate run 1; ask 3 gates any archiving or deletion; asks 4–7 resolve on silence, each by the default stated with it." (Paragraph 1.) Minor caveat: this sentence lives in "The answer first," not in the Asks section itself — the ask set proper never restates which of its members gate.

## Stumbles in reading order

1. **"5 awaiting rulings" (ask 1) is never linked to ask 6.** I had to count ask 6's records myself (a=1, b=1, c=3) to verify the 5 reconcile. The 6 scenario pins get an explicit "ask 6c below" pointer; the 5 records don't.
2. **"Ask 1 fixes which records are kept, retired, or terminal, the run order, and the rewrite-family groupings as nominations only"** — reread required: does "as nominations only" scope over all three list items or just the family groupings? If keep/retire/terminal is *fixed* by ask 1, ask 6's separate rulings on five of those records sit in tension; if it's all nominations, "fixes" is the wrong verb.
3. **Counting the "four" in ask 2** takes parsing: one amended process, one new process, two new data types — the enumeration is buried in prose ("New: … and its two supporting data types") and I counted twice.

6. **`verified-by: pending`** in front-matter only makes sense after reaching the last Deferred bullet — a forward reference, resolved 130 lines later.

## Overload verdict

**Yes — rulable in one short sitting.** ~140 lines, seven asks of which four (3, 4, 5, 7) are fully self-contained policy choices, two (1, 2) reduce to trusting a stated verification, and one (6) is three small calls. Paragraph 1 gives a single-sentence fast path, defaults make silence safe, and the gating sentence tells the reader the minimum ruling (asks 1–3) needed to unblock work. ## Top three changes

1. **Close the census loop in ask 1:** point "5 awaiting rulings" at ask 6 explicitly, and rewrite "fixes … as nominations only" to say unambiguously which classifications block-approval makes final and which remain nominations.
2. **Give 6b's orphaned behavior a landing spot:** name where the as-built certificate-authority behavior "gets its decision fresh" (a filed backlog item, mirroring 6c, or the run-2 open-item list) so retiring the record doesn't leave live code undocumented on a promise.
3. **Put the gating sentence on the ask set itself:** repeat "gates run 1 / gates archiving / resolves on silence" as a tag on each ask header (or a line atop the Asks section), so the resolution rules travel with the asks rather than only in the preamble.

# Brief 026 — Rebaseline migration: rule on rev 3 and its preconditions

## The answer first

You returned the migration plan with findings, and the adversarial
review you directed found worse defects underneath — repairs for all of
them are now landed as drafts on `main`, so what remains is your
ruling. **Recommendation: approve the plan (ask 1) and the four
repaired definitions (ask 2), ratify the archive contract (ask 3), and
let asks 4–7 resolve by their stated defaults.** Asks 1 and 2 gate
run 1; ask 3 gates any archiving or deletion; asks 4–7 resolve on
silence, each by the default stated with it. Nothing is retired,
deleted, or rewritten by silence alone.

The three worst defects found and repaired: the approved migration
process had a broken step flow (a step with no exit before your review
loop — no rewrite could ever have run); the 163 retiring records had no
process that moves them; and record collapses were being decided before
any definition existed to license them.

The shape of the migration: six scheduled entries — five
definition-building runs (run 1 architecture principles, run 2
decision records, run 3 framework spec, run 4 PM records, run 5
findings) plus a mechanical scenario close-out. Each run first builds
and proves its type's definition ("chain": typedef, guideline, fitness
set, process, roles, compiled skill), takes your review of the chain
plus one real rewritten exemplar (up to 3 rounds, then it parks), and
mass-rewrites only after your approval. The definitions do not
pre-exist — building them is each run's first act, and the plan now
says so. Ask 1 fixes which records are kept, retired, or terminal, the
run order, and the rewrite-family groupings as nominations only; final
record granularity (your "collapsing many into 15 overloads a decision
